record: Joined 40 attorneys general opposing a proposed 10-year federal ban on state enforcement of AI laws.
South Dakota Attorney General press release, 16 May 2025
Joined a 44-state attorneys general letter demanding AI companies protect children from harmful chatbot interactions.
Joined a bipartisan 40-attorney-general filing in the Character.AI bankruptcy seeking protection of user data and child safety.
grade_reason: As South Dakota Attorney General he has spoken about AI repeatedly, including in 2026, but only about children's safety, fraud, privacy and state regulatory power; nothing found acknowledges catastrophic risk.
notes: 8 web searches ran, none refused. No campaign site found and no statements found on superintelligence, extinction, loss of control, a pause, China talks or self-improving AI. As a representative-elect he could not have co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act and did not sign the House letters. A PBS Books segment 'Seeking Common Ground: Artificial Intelligence with Attorney General Marty Jackley' (12 February 2025, https://www.wgbh.org/tv-shows/book-view-now/seeking-common-ground-artificial-intelligence-with-attorney-general-marty-jackley-pcbi8q) was found, but the page has only a paraphrase (he wants AI used legitimately and not to defraud citizens), so it is left out of statements. The 16 May 2025 quote is the first part of a longer sentence; the fetch tool did not return the whole sentence verbatim, so only the opening clause is quoted and the listed harms are given in context. Searches also returned older items (2023-2024: AI child sexual abuse material legislation, AI robocalls) outside the period.
